s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with cerebellar and brainstem involvement
salient_findings: Morning headaches with nausea and vomiting
Numbness, tingling, and weakness in upper extremities
Blurred or double vision, vertigo, and clumsy gait
Vertical and horizontal nystagmus and gait ataxia
key_facts: 2-month history of progressively worsening symptoms
No significant past medical history
Headaches did not fully resolve with analgesics
Numbness, tingling, and weakness in both upper extremities
Intermittent blurred or double vision, vertigo, and clumsy gait
Normal cranial nerve function except for nystagmus
Mildly hypodense mass lesion in the fourth ventricle region
Surrounding brain edema and obstructive hydrocephalus
Mass caused effacement of the fourth-ventricle outlets, cerebellar compression, and tonsillar herniation

shortlist.label: Medulloblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location in the fourth ventricle and symptoms of cerebellar and brainstem involvement

shortlist.label: Ependymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common location in the fourth ventricle and potential for causing obstructive hydrocephalus

shortlist.label: Choroid plexus papilloma
shortlist.why_kept: Typical location in the fourth ventricle and potential for causing hydrocephalus

shortlist.label: Pilocytic astrocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common in young adults and potential for causing symptoms due to location in the cerebellum or brainstem

shortlist.label: Subependymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location in the fourth ventricle and potential for causing obstructive hydrocephalus

shortlist.label: Hemangioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Potential for causing symptoms due to location in the cerebellum or brainstem

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Potential for causing symptoms due to location near the cerebellum or brainstem

shortlist.label: Choroid plexus carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive nature and potential for causing rapid decline in neurological function

raw.rationale: The tumor's location in the fourth ventricle and its well-demarcated, homogeneous appearance on MRI are consistent with ependymoma, which often arises from the ependymal lining of the ventricles and can cause obstructive hydrocephalus and cerebellar compression.

rejected.label: Medulloblastoma
rejected.why: Typically more heterogeneous and aggressive in appearance on imaging

rejected.label: Choroid plexus papilloma
rejected.why: Usually has a more cauliflower-like appearance and is often associated with calcifications

rejected.label: Pilocytic astrocytoma
rejected.why: Typically has a more cystic appearance with a mural nodule and is often associated with a more gradual onset of symptoms

rejected.label: Subependymoma
rejected.why: Usually occurs in older adults and has a more discrete, nodular appearance

rejected.label: Hemangioblastoma
rejected.why: Typically has a more cystic appearance with a highly vascular mural nodule and is often associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Usually occurs in older adults and has a more dural-based appearance

rejected.label: Choroid plexus carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically has a more aggressive appearance on imaging and is often associated with a more rapid onset of symptoms
